customer: Hello, I'm hoping to trade in my hatchback for something roomier, but the car is in both my name and my partner's. Could you tell me whether we both need to be there to sell it? Thank you for your help!
agent: Thanks for reaching out, and congratulations on moving up to a bigger car! According to our article "When more than one person owns the car," every listed owner has to sign the sale documents, and the easiest way is for both of you to come to the appraisal appointment with your photo IDs. If your partner can't make it, they can sign a power of attorney, form NW-POA-1, which must be notarized. It also helps to check your title: if your names are joined by 'and,' both of you need to sign, but if they're joined by 'or,' only one signature is needed.
